I have experience with Python and AI/ML concepts, and I’m eager to explore how technology and scientific data can be used to address challenges related to Earth and space.
summary:
FireSafe Space is an interactive, AI-powered dashboard that summarizes, ranks and interprets NASA’s microgravity combustion investigations for human space exploration fire safety.

NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository holds years of ISS flame experiments, but the data is hard to find, compare and interpret. Our dashboard organizes 14 investigations (including BASS, SAME, FLEX and ACME) by fuel, oxygen level, airflow, hardware and measurements, with key findings from NASA fact sheets.

Users choose a need, such as a Moon base, spacecraft, fire detection or suppression, and the dashboard ranks the most relevant experiments using transparent, adjustable scores. It also compares investigations, highlights gaps such as the missing partial-gravity data, and lets users ask questions in plain language, answered by an AI model (Gemini) from the experiment database.

This matters because Moon habitats are expected to use 30% or more oxygen, which makes materials far more flammable. Clearer fire safety knowledge helps protect future crews and also benefits fire safety on Earth.
details:
FireSafe Space is a web dashboard built on a curated database of 14 NASA microgravity combustion investigations (BASS, BASS-II, BASS-M, SAME, FLEX and ACME experiments, among others). Each entry lists fuel, oxygen level, airflow, hardware, measurements and key findings. Users pick a need, such as a Moon base, fire detection or suppression, and the app ranks investigations with a transparent weighted score across eight criteria. Weights can be adjusted. Users can compare experiments on a radar chart, see where research is missing, and ask questions in plain language. An AI model (Gemini) answers only from the database, and a built-in scoring engine works when no AI key is available.

Benefits and impact: It saves researchers and students time finding the right experiment, and it points out gaps such as the lack of partial-gravity (lunar) data in PSI. It supports safer Moon habitats, where 30%+ oxygen makes materials more flammable, and it links space fire research to Earth benefits like smoke detectors and firefighter gear.

Tools: Python, Streamlit, pandas, Plotly, Gemini API, GitHub and Streamlit Community Cloud. Data came from NASA’s combustion science fact sheets and the PSI resources. We used an AI assistant (Claude) to help write and debug code.

Creativity and factors considered: Rankings change with the user’s mission need, scores are open and editable, and entries are marked verified or unverified. 8 of 14 are verified against NASA fact sheets. Limitations: scores are our own judgments, and we did not process raw PSI data files.
